housing.summary: Madrid's rental market is competitive, especially in central districts (Centro, Salamanca, Chamberi). One-bedroom apartments in the centre are in high demand; expect to provide proof of income and often a guarantor. Idealista and Fotocasa are the dominant rental portals.

banking.summary: Opening a Spanish bank account typically requires an NIE (foreigner ID number), passport, proof of address (empadronamiento) and proof of employment or income. Major retail banks include BBVA, Santander, CaixaBank and Sabadell; non-resident accounts are available at most branches before an NIE is issued.

schools.summary: Madrid offers a wide range of public (Spanish curriculum), bilingual, concertado (semi-private) and international schools. International options cover British, American, French, German and IB curricula, concentrated in the northern and western suburbs (e.g. Pozuelo, Las Rozas, Aravaca).

legal_admin.summary: New residents must register on the municipal register (empadronamiento) at their local Junta Municipal or Padron office to obtain the certificado de empadronamiento, which is required for many administrative steps. EU citizens register with the Central Register of Foreigners; non-EU nationals need the appropriate residence permit and TIE card.
legal_admin.registration_step: Empadronamiento (registration on the padron municipal at the local Ayuntamiento office)

tax_finance.summary: Individuals need a tax identification number to work and pay taxes: the NIE serves as the tax ID for foreigners, while Spanish nationals use the DNI/NIF. Income tax (IRPF) is administered nationally by the Agencia Tributaria (AEAT), with regional components applied by the Comunidad de Madrid.

transport.summary: Madrid has an extensive integrated public transport network (metro, buses, Cercanias commuter rail and light rail) managed by the Consorcio Regional de Transportes de Madrid (CRTM). A rechargeable Tarjeta Transporte Publico is used for the Abono Transportes monthly pass. Under-26s pay a heavily discounted youth pass.
transport.network_name: Consorcio Regional de Transportes de Madrid (CRTM)
transport.driving_licence_exchange: EU/EEA licences are valid; many non-EU licences must be exchanged for a Spanish licence within 6 months of residency, depending on bilateral agreements (via DGT).
transport.healthcare_registration: Register for public healthcare by obtaining a social security number and registering with a local health centre (centro de salud) under the Comunidad de Madrid SERMAS to receive a tarjeta sanitaria.
